Telescope 3.6 gives the desktop app a new look and makes streaming a lot smoother when the Wi-Fi isn't great.

## New

**A new look.** The desktop window got rebuilt card by card. Checkboxes are switches now, resolution and frame rate are tiles you click and every card has its own colour. If you liked everything purple there's **Card colours** in Advanced that switches it to **Monochrome**. Advanced, Keyboard shortcuts and Plugins use one row per setting with the longer explanations moved into tooltips (which got shorter and friendlier too). A few buttons and labels got new names along the way (like **Mirror** and **Upside down**). It also works a lot better from the keyboard. Tab goes through the window in the order you read it, focus rings only show up when you're actually using the keyboard and every control has a name for screen readers.

**UDP on Wi-Fi (experimental).** A new switch in the Connection card sends Light over UDP instead of TCP while the phone is on Wi-Fi. When the network is busy a lost packet then only means that one piece gets sent again, where TCP holds up the whole stream until it arrives. It's encrypted like everything else between the phone and the computer. If nothing gets through (usually a firewall) Telescope goes back to TCP automatically. It doesn't work with Dynamic or Heavy yet. My own Wi-Fi is too quiet to show much of a difference so I'd really like to hear how it does on a crowded network.

**Hardware acceleration.** Advanced has a switch for decoding Light on the graphics card instead of the processor. It's off by default and mostly worth it at 4K or on a laptop, since a desktop processor handles 1080p easily. Linux with an NVIDIA card works right away. AMD and Intel cards on Linux need VA-API which the PyAV Telescope installs doesn't have, so **Set up VA-API…** next to the switch either uses your distro's PyAV or builds one for you in about a minute. If a system update breaks that build later, setup notices it and offers a **Rebuild** button. It should work on Windows with any graphics card too, but I don't have a Windows PC with a real graphics card to try it on so please report it if it doesn't. If decoding on the graphics card ever fails Telescope moves back to the processor for the rest of the run.

**Auto level for the mic.** A new switch in the Microphone card evens out quiet and loud speech. It stops adjusting while nobody's talking so the room noise doesn't get turned up in the pauses. Off by default.

## Smoother streaming

- The mic stops clicking when the phone's clock and the computer's drift apart. It starts with less delay too (20 ms over USB, 40 ms over Wi-Fi), and extra delay that piled up after a Wi-Fi hiccup gets dropped in the next pause.
- Plugging the cable in mid-stream (with Connect via on Automatic) moves video and mic over to USB without a gap. **Switch to USB** only shows up when that didn't work.
- The phone now asks for H.264's High profile, which looks a bit sharper at the same bitrate. Phones that don't support it stay on Baseline like before.
- Dynamic copes better with really slow links. It goes down to 0.3 Mbps, jumps straight to a frame rate that fits and doesn't restart the camera each time.
- Phones that support it spread keyframes out instead of sending a big one every second, which made the bitrate jump up and down.
- A phone that's getting too hot lowers its frame rate to 24 and then 15 fps and goes back to 30 once it cools down. Before this it kept heating up until the heat alert stopped the stream. From Android 11 it reacts to Android's own heat forecast before it actually gets that hot.
- Streams start about 0.1 s sooner and come back about a second sooner after the Wi-Fi drops. Losing Wi-Fi also stops showing the "Can't keep up" banner (it's a dropped link, not a slow one).
- When the phone's signal is weak or it's on 2.4 GHz, "Can't keep up" mentions that (moving closer or a 5 GHz network helps more than lowering the quality there). Copy diagnostics now includes the phone's Wi-Fi.

## Phone app

Most of the streaming changes above need the 3.6 phone app, so update it too (the desktop offers that over USB when the phone is plugged in). From now on it's best to always keep the phone app and the desktop on the same version.

- The screen stays on while Telescope is open because Android only keeps Wi-Fi at full speed with the screen on. Pressing the power button still turns it off and the stream keeps going.
- While streaming over Wi-Fi the phone keeps its Wi-Fi out of power saving (which caused short lag spikes).
- The mic comes back when Android's audio system restarts. It used to stay quiet until the next stream.
- If the app was opened while a closing copy still held its port, computers couldn't find it until you switched away and back. It keeps trying now.

## Fixed

- Stopping the stream on the phone and leaving the app right away no longer shows up on the desktop as a dropped stream.
- Saved keyboard shortcuts and panning with the arrow keys work again.
- Fixed a crash that could come from the keyboard shortcuts plugin.
- Wait screen, Keyboard shortcuts and Wait before stopping open on top of the main window and Plugins no longer blocks every other window.
- An error from Advanced (a failed driver reload, for example) shows up right under that row in Advanced with the command to copy. It used to only be a banner in the main window.
- The Pan readout shows H and V on separate lines so -100% fits.

Found something broken? Open an issue and paste your **Copy diagnostics** report into it.
